title: Touring Europe with George Lewis: countries and television
summary: Anders asks about his first trip to Europe with George Lewis, England, Scandinavia, Germany and TV.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Why don't we get Anders over here, and we can talk about Europe for a while. He can maybe question you about Europe better than I can. Oh, I see.
He's going to do the interview.
He's going to do the interview. And I'll watch the machine. Just sit down there and you can ask him about Europe.
Want me to start right now? Yeah, anytime.
Oh, you want to? No, just ask him about Europe, not just Denmark but England too. Anything you know about over there.
When was your first chance to go to Europe?
Well the time that I came with George, that's my first chance to go with George Lewis.
Jazz band. Jazz band, yeah. You saw quite a few of the European countries, didn't you?
Oh, I saw a great deal of them.
Playing in England for a long time?
Well we played in England about three or four weeks.
And which other countries do you remember the name of them?
Well, I'll never forget Denmark, that's for sure, in Sweden. And you went to Germany too, didn't you?
Yeah, that was close. I think you made about, as far as I remember, you made about ten concerts in Germany, didn't you?
Well, no, we didn't do concerts.
We did a television show. Oh yeah, that's right. You just made it to a, George stayed a little after you left.
Well yeah, George, yeah, he joined up with Kent's band.
Yeah, that's right. And then he toured alone. That's right.
Who's Kent? Which one is it? Kent Collier.
Kent Collier, the British trumpet player. Yeah, that's right. So you played both in concerts and television, clubs as far as I remember?
Yeah, we played mostly concerts. Yeah. But when we went to Germany, well we did mostly rehearsing for about four or five days for the show.
Was that your first television experience? Oh no. You've been doing television before?
The television here, New York and Los Angeles and San Francisco.
Was it very different to do television in Europe?
No, it was okay. It was okay. It was one thing, but like all the stations, the lights, it was tough.
